items.title: T2 Blood and T2 Gray Matter parameters are accepted but never used in the computation

findings.title: T2 Blood and T2 Gray Matter parameters are accepted but never used in the computation
findings.evidence:
data = ASLData(
   pcasl=args.asl, m0=args.m0, ld_values=ld, pld_values=pld, te_values=te,
   average_m0=True
   )
findings.explanation: `args.t2b` and `args.t2gm` are parsed from the CLI (lines 245-246) and echoed in the verbose output (lines 108-109), but neither ASLData nor MultiTE_ASLMapping receives them; the only other occurrences in the file are those four lines. A user who changes 'T2 Blood (ms)' or 'T2 Gray Matter (ms)' in the GUI gets identical results, silently, which for a quantitative mapping tool can lead to misinterpreted output values.
findings.suggestion: Pass the T2 values to the reconstruction (e.g. as arguments to MultiTE_ASLMapping/create_map) or remove the parameters from the XML so users are not misled.

items.title: asltk installed into Slicer's shared Python environment at module run without user confirmation

findings.title: asltk installed into Slicer's shared Python environment at module run without user confirmation
findings.explanation: The identical block exists in Multi_Echo_ASL/Multi_Echo_ASL.py:32-34. The first time a user runs either module, the script silently pip-installs `asltk==1.1.3` (plus its transitive dependencies) into the Slicer Python environment shared by all extensions and by users who never open this module. There is no confirmation dialog and no progress/size information; the only disclosure is a sentence in README.md:14 and docs/index.md:69. The exact `==1.1.3` pin can also force a specific version of a dependency that Slicer bundles (numpy/scipy/nibabel class packages) if asltk declares one, which can break other extensions.
findings.suggestion: Ask the user before installing (e.g. a qt.QMessageBox / ctk confirmation in the module, or ship the dependency via the extension build), avoid exact pins of packages Slicer bundles, and state the download size and target environment in the prompt.

findings.title: Runtime pip install of asltk into Slicer's shared Python environment without user confirmation
findings.explanation: When asltk is missing, the module silently installs a pinned package and its transitive dependencies into the shared Slicer environment, affecting other extensions and users who never open the module. Nothing asks for consent, and failures are not handled. The same pattern is in Multi_Echo_ASL/Multi_Echo_ASL.py lines 32-34. The transitive dependency set was not verified, so conflicts or bundled Qt/VTK/torch packages are possible.
findings.suggestion: Ask the user for confirmation before installing, show the package list, handle pip failures with a clear message, and prefer declaring the dependency in the extension's install step or documentation. Verify asltk's transitive dependencies against Slicer-bundled packages.

items.title: Catalog tracks moving branch 'main' rather than a fixed revision

findings.title: Catalog tracks moving branch 'main' rather than a fixed revision
findings.evidence: set(EXTENSION_DEPENDS "NA") # Specified as a list or "NA" if no dependencies
findings.explanation: The catalog entry sets scm_revision to 'main', so the code built by the index can change without review. Per policy this is not a finding by itself, but the reviewed commit b805616 is not pinned.
findings.suggestion: Pin scm_revision to the reviewed commit or a release tag for reproducible builds.

items.title: Default brain mask is a numpy array while a user mask is an ImageIO object

findings.title: Default brain mask is a numpy array while a user mask is an ImageIO object
findings.explanation: `recon.set_brain_mask(mask_img)` therefore receives two different types depending on whether a mask was supplied, and the default path assumes a 5-D ASL array (indexing [0,0,:,:,:]) which raises IndexError for 4-D input. Same pattern in Multi_Echo_ASL.py:66-68.
findings.suggestion: Build the default mask from the M0 image geometry as an ImageIO-compatible object and derive the shape without hard-coded 5-D indexing.

items.title: Empty license element in module descriptors

findings.title: Empty <license/> element in both module XML files
findings.explanation: The repository has a valid MIT LICENSE and MIT headers in the scripts, but the CLI metadata shown in Slicer's module information panel is empty, so users do not see the terms where they look for them. Same in Multi_Echo_ASL/Multi_Echo_ASL.xml:14.
findings.suggestion: Fill in the license field (e.g. 'MIT') in both XML files.

findings.title: Empty license element in module descriptors
findings.explanation: The module XML lists no license, while the root LICENSE file is MIT. This is a descriptive inconsistency only and does not block distribution.
findings.suggestion: Fill in the license element with MIT to match the LICENSE file.

items.title: No automated tests and documentation inconsistencies

findings.title: No automated tests and documentation inconsistencies
findings.evidence: <description><![CDATA[The T2 value for the blood. By default, the value of 75 ms is assumed.]]></description>
findings.explanation: The t2gm parameter description says 'blood' when it refers to gray matter. No unit tests or sample-data test cases are present in the repository, so regressions in the CLI parsing and validation logic are not caught. The README image points to the develop branch while CMake uses main.
findings.suggestion: Fix the t2gm description, add tests for argument parsing and validation, and align documentation branch references.

items.title: No tests, no clinical-use disclaimer, sample data hosted externally without stated license

findings.title: No tests, no clinical-use disclaimer, sample data hosted externally without stated license
findings.evidence: 1. Download the sample data (hosted at a [public link from Google Drive](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1agtHY9SLvC9975L6H0RL6PfIHATnJKcI/view))
findings.explanation: The repository contains no test or self-test, and the tutorial depends on a Google Drive file whose license/redistribution terms are not stated. Quantitative CBF/ATT maps are clinically suggestive, but neither the README nor the module XML carries a research-use-only disclaimer.
findings.suggestion: Add a short self-test or sample-data download through Slicer's Sample Data mechanism, state the sample-data license, and add a research-use-only notice.

items.title: Output folder is validated but never used; XML text about a home-directory default is misleading

findings.title: Output folder is validated but never used; XML text about a home-directory default is misleading
findings.explanation: `out_folder` is only checked for existence (line 148) and never used to build output paths; outputs go to the paths Slicer passes for the output image nodes. The XML description (CBF_ATT_ASL.xml:11) tells users the home directory is used when --outputFolder is omitted, which does not match the code.
findings.suggestion: Either use out_folder to resolve relative output names or remove the parameter and the corresponding description text.

findings.title: outputFolder argument is parsed but never applied to output paths
findings.explanation: out_folder is only validated. Output files are written to out_cbf and out_att exactly as given (lines 130-133), so a relative output name is resolved against the process working directory. The XML description (CBF_ATT_ASL.xml lines 8-11) says the home directory is assumed when outputFolder is absent, which does not match what the code does. Multi_Echo_ASL.py has the same gap.
findings.suggestion: Join output file names with out_folder when they are relative, or correct the documentation.

items.title: Smoothing-parameter validation in the CBF module can never trigger

findings.title: Smoothing-parameter validation in the CBF module can never trigger
findings.explanation: The XML enumeration supplies 'None'/'Gaussian'/'Median' (CBF_ATT_ASL.xml:96-98), so the lowercase comparisons at lines 187 and 192 are always False and invalid sigma/kernel values (e.g. sigma <= 0, even median size) reach asltk unchecked. Multi_Echo_ASL.py:192,197 uses the correct capitalisation, so the two modules behave differently.
findings.suggestion: Compare against 'Gaussian'/'Median' (or lower-case args.smoothMethod once, as is done at line 81).

findings.title: Smoothing parameter validation compares against wrong-case value and never fires for CBF
findings.explanation: The GUI passes 'Gaussian' (CBF XML line 97), but the check compares against lowercase 'gaussian', so a non-positive sigma is not rejected here. Downstream code may then fail or produce wrong output. Multi_Echo_ASL.py uses the correct capitalized comparison on line 192.
findings.suggestion: Compare against 'Gaussian' and 'Median' consistently, or normalize case before validation.

items.title: requirements.txt pins a different asltk version than the code installs

findings.title: requirements.txt pins a different asltk version than the code installs
findings.explanation: The documentation build (readthedocs) installs asltk 1.1.0 while both modules install 1.1.3 at runtime, so the documented API and the executed API can diverge; the file is also not used by the CMake build, so it is easy to leave stale.
findings.suggestion: Keep a single version pin shared by requirements.txt and the pip_install call.

findings.title: asltk version mismatch between runtime install and requirements.txt
findings.explanation: The modules install asltk==1.1.3 at runtime (CBF_ATT_ASL.py line 34, Multi_Echo_ASL.py line 34), but requirements.txt pins asltk==1.1.0. Documentation and the tested version are therefore unclear, which makes reproducibility harder.
findings.suggestion: Align requirements.txt and the runtime pin, and record the tested asltk version in the docs.

items.title: rich.print interprets bracketed text in messages as markup

findings.title: rich.print interprets bracketed text in messages as markup
findings.explanation: `print` is replaced by rich's markup-aware version, so messages such as the validation text at line 184 containing `['None', 'Gaussian', 'Median']` or file paths containing '[' are parsed as style tags and can raise a markup/style error instead of printing the diagnostic, hiding the real error from the user.
findings.suggestion: Use rich.print with markup=False (or the builtin print) for diagnostics and for echoing user-supplied paths.
